items.title: SOMA: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Behavior and Body-Motion Understanding
items.summary: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. Yet current evaluations of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) largely focus on objects, scenes, and coarse actions, leaving their ability to reason about the body itself poorly assessed. This is especially challenging from the egocentric perspective, in which the body is only partially visible and motion must be inferred from occluded and temporally distributed cues. We introduce SOMA, a benchmark for fine-grained body-motion understanding from egocentric video, comprising 1,632 human-verif…

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the…

items.title: AuditFL: A Contract-Backed Clearing Layer for Open Federated Learning
items.summary: Federated learning (FL) keeps raw data local, but most deployments still rely on a trusted coordinator for client admission, checkpoint distribution, update collection, aggregation, and rewards. This paper presents AuditFL, a contract-backed clearing layer for auditable FL in open settings. AuditFL keeps training and aggregation off chain, stores model artifacts in an assumed reliable off-chain artifact store, and records only content identifiers and economic state on chain. items.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
items.summary: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful. Because this safety-degrading data looks benign, standard content filters struggle to catch it. We tackle this problem by developing SimpleLoRIF, a scalable gradient embedding method that identifies fine-tuning examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior. items.title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
items.summary: Do research agents have taste, the judgment of which experiments are worth running before their outcomes are known? We give six frontier models seven recent NLP papers. items.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
items.summary: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. items.title: Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report
items.summary: Metis is a bet that better data, better training methods and new architectures can buy what a bigger parameter count cannot, at a fraction of the cost. Metis-1.6 is its latest step: two language models built from scratch by a single researcher, Praxis (2.94B parameters, 0.46B active per pass) and Logos (10.23B parameters, 1.18B active per pass). Both run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention mixture-of-experts stack twice for every token, so each token gets a second look. items.title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
items.summary: An effective agent memory system should adapt to a user's history and task requirements. Human-annotated supervision can guide this adaptation by providing feedback for evaluating and improving memory designs. Yet suitable labels are rarely available for new user histories, and manually constructing QA pairs and supporting evidence is costly. We introduce MemSteer, which turns unlabeled user histories into question-answer (QA) supervision with supporting evidence for memory-design optimization. items.title: VoxLock: Target-Speaker Extraction for Voice Agents Without an Enrollment Step
items.summary: A voice agent's speech recognizer transcribes everyone near the microphone, including people other than the caller. items.summary: Large language model agents are increasingly used for scientific discovery. However, existing benchmarks mix law inference with programming, score data fitting instead of prediction on unseen inputs, and do not separate empirical evidence from pretrained priors. We introduce SciGame, a controlled benchmark that converts scientific literature into structured scientific cards. items.summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to recover well-exposed and perceptually faithful images from severely degraded observations. items.summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. items.summary: Edge medical segmentation must reconcile small model size, high accuracy, and fast inference. TernScope addresses this tradeoff through model--hardware co-design, learning a compact segmentation network whose low-bit operators also simplify hardware execution. Split-channel large-kernel blocks preserve spatial context with limited computation, while branch fusion removes redundant inference paths. items.summary: Existing sketch generation methods often rely on image guidance and are largely limited to individual objects or simplified scenes, leaving text-guided complex scene sketching underexplored. items.summary: Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. items.summary: Proactive agents must decide whether, when, and how far to assist without an explicit request. Existing evaluations often rely on automated scores or binary verdicts, offering limited human diagnosis of evidence use and intervention quality. items.title: 前公司老板找我回去救场，情况比较特殊，想听听各位的建议
items.summary: # 求助：前老板邀约回去救场，想请教大家风险和谈判要点 各位好，想咨询下大家的经验。 ## 背景 我是技术出身的产品经理，之前一手搭建整套产研团队，负责的产品已经多端稳定上线。一个月前正常离职，交接工作当时处理得比较完整。 现在前老板联系我，说产研团队军心涣散、普遍摆烂，项目和系统已经接近系统性崩溃，希望我回去接手稳住局面。 ## 核心顾虑/风险点 1. 公司之前存在晚发薪资+月底缴纳社保的记录； 2. 团队制度近期变动：调整为单休、强抓考勤、新增 KPI ，内部氛围偏向变相倒逼员工主动离职； 3. 角色尴尬：回去后大概率要当“背锅+坏人”，需要推动整改、梳理问题、压进度，很容易和老部下、现有同事形成对立。 我对之前带出来的团队和产品有感情，但不想踩坑。想请教大家： 如果考虑回去，在**谈条件、权责边界、劳动合同、风险隔离、团队沟通、止损预案**这些方面，有哪些必须提前敲定、重点留意的事项？ 另外也想听听大家判断：这种局面本身值不值得接？ 感谢各位分享经验。

items.title: 朋友一家定期献血，我看着矿泉水瓶陷入了沉思
items.summary: 有个朋友在血站工作，听他说，他们家里人都会定期献血。 这让我有点好奇：以前听人说，定期献血能促进造血，让血液“更新”，对身体有好处；也有人觉得，献血会让身体变虚，需要很久才能恢复。 这两种说法到底哪个更靠谱？ 我自己一想到一次献血 400 毫升，就有点发怵——差不多是一瓶 500 毫升矿泉水的八成。想象一下从身体里抽出这么多血，总觉得自己可能会头晕 😂 你献过血吗？一次献了多少？

items.title: agent 的代码到底审不审核
items.summary: 用 claude code 写的代码 ``` # 子集聚合全部改成掩码列，取代循环里的 kills/killed/npc/rev/paid 五次切片 d["_paid"] = ((d["is_revive"] == 1) & (d["irevivemoney"] > 0)).astype(int) d["_kill_tgt"] = d["votherroleid"].where(d["is_kill"] == 1) d["_killed_src"] = d["votherroleid"].where(d["is_killed_by_role"] == 1) d["_rev_type"] = d["irevivetype"].where(d["is_revive"] == 1) d["_paid_money"] = d["irevivemoney"].where(d["_paid"] == 1) d["_red"] = (utils.to_num(d["ikilledred"]).fillna(0) if has_killedred else pd.Series(0.0, index=d.index)) gb = d.groupby("roleid", sort=False) ``` 全是这样的，完全看不懂！但是让 agent 讲解一看，确实又高效又简洁，但是很难看懂啊。到底审还是不…
